dse_runs.notes: Bursty 8-channel sensor offload: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, Poisson at 2 requests/us, p99 latency <= 0.4 us, err <= 2^-10, min LUTs+FFs. Prior campaign: iterative family dominated the front (data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=1, rounding=round won for a low-rate area-min spec); pipelined/pipelined_m/unrolled_k never reached a front. Cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% low. For p99 latency, a single iterative CORDIC with ~12 iters at ~150 MHz is ~80 ns per request; 8 back-to-back requests = ~640 ns > 0.4 us p99 bound, so the system sim will likely need higher throughput (pipelined or unrolled) or a faster clock. Prioritize designs with enough throughput to drain 8-request bursts within 0.4 us p99, while keeping area low.

final_text: Campaign complete — the single spec **bursty_offload** is finalized. L1 (400 evals, structured DSE graph) mapped a 39-design feasible Pareto front dominated by pipelined_m variants (m=3–8); the iterative family couldn't drain 8-request bursts within the 0.4 µs p99 bound, and pipelined/unrolled_k stayed off the front as in prior campaigns. L2 SimPy simulation of the top 5 confirmed all pass, with the winner's p99 rising from the 0.112 µs analytic bound to 0.135 µs simulated. L3/L4 had no recorded measurements for this design (fresh W=15 verification too heavy for a live run; no recorded synthesis), so back_annotate had nothing to compare and no winner change was flagged. Final selection: **pipelined_m:data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=0, rounding=round, m=4** — estimated 813 LUTs+FFs (620 LUTs / 194 FFs), 97.8 MSPS, error 2^-10.23, simulated p99 latency 0.135 µs. A lesson note was stored for future bursty-latency specs.
